keyPoints: 首段提出观点：关键在选什么工作、投入多少时间。
正面论述从获得经验和理解赚钱不易两方面展开。
同时承认风险，体现辩证思考。
结尾给出具体建议：与兴趣相关、限定时长。

items.title: How People Spend Their Leisure Time
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the pie chart below, which shows how urban residents spend their leisure time. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
items.reference:
The pie chart shows how urban residents in China spend their spare time. Watching short videos and playing games take the largest share, followed by sports, while reading and other activities account for a smaller part.

This distribution is easy to understand. Short videos and games are cheap, convenient and immediately entertaining: a tired office worker can relax with a phone for ten minutes without leaving his seat. Sports require equipment, time and energy, so they attract fewer people, though the number is growing as health becomes a bigger concern. Reading demands quiet and concentration, which are hard to find in a busy day.

The chart suggests a warning as well as a description. Leisure should help us recover, not simply consume our attention. If most free time disappears into a screen, people may feel tired rather than refreshed. A reasonable balance might be to keep some time for exercise and for a book, so that leisure restores both the body and the mind.
keyPoints: 第一段概述饼图各部分占比，不逐一列举数字。
第二段分析原因，用 cheap / convenient / demands quiet 等表述。
第三段提出评价与建议，避免只描述不评论。
注意非谓语与从句的正确使用，句式要有变化。

items.title: We Are What We Repeatedly Do
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the saying 'We are what we repeatedly do.' You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
The remark that we are what we repeatedly do points to a simple but powerful truth: character is not shaped by occasional heroic efforts but by daily habits.

Consider two students of similar ability. One spends twenty minutes every evening reviewing his notes; the other studies intensively the night before an exam. In the short term, the second may seem efficient. Over a term, however, the first builds a body of knowledge that cannot be assembled overnight and, more importantly, he builds the habit of steady work. The difference between them is not talent but repetition. The same is true of health, of friendship and even of honesty: small choices, made again and again, gradually become who we are.

This insight is both encouraging and demanding. It is encouraging because it means we do not need extraordinary moments to change our lives; a better routine, repeated patiently, is enough. It is demanding because it leaves us no excuse: every day we are quietly voting for the person we are becoming. If we wish to be diligent, kind or reliable, the way is not to wait for inspiration but to act that way repeatedly, until it becomes natural.
keyPoints: 开头解释名言含义，提出“品格由日常习惯塑造”的中心论点。
用两个学生的学习方式作对比，使论证具体可感。
结尾从“鼓励”和“要求”两面展开，深化观点。
引用名言时保持原句措辞不变。

items.title: Skills or Grades?
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on whether employers should value practical skills more than academic grades. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
When employers recruit new staff, should they attach more weight to practical skills than to academic grades? In my view, grades still matter, but they should not be the deciding factor.

Grades are useful because they are comparable and relatively objective. A strong record suggests that a candidate can absorb complex material and meet deadlines under pressure. For professions such as medicine or engineering, where a mistake can be costly, this evidence cannot be ignored.

Nevertheless, grades measure only one kind of ability. A graduate with excellent marks may still be poor at explaining ideas, resolving conflicts or adapting to an unexpected situation, while a student with average grades may have run a small business, organised a campus event or completed a demanding internship. Such experience shows qualities that no examination can capture. Employers who hire only on paper risk employing people who are good at exams but poor at work.

The sensible approach is to treat grades as a threshold rather than a final answer. Once a candidate's academic level is acceptable, practical skills, attitude and potential deserve greater attention. After all, a company needs colleagues who can get things done, not merely people with good marks.
keyPoints: 开头用问句引出话题，随即亮明“成绩重要但非决定因素”的立场。
先承认成绩的可比性与客观性，再指出其局限，体现让步论证。
用 average grades 但经验丰富的学生作反例，避免片面。
结尾提出可操作的判断标准：把成绩当门槛。

items.title: The Rise of Remote Work
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the chart below, which shows that the proportion of employees working from home in a large city has grown noticeably over the past eight years. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
The chart shows that the proportion of employees working from home in a large city has grown noticeably over the past eight years. This shift deserves attention because it changes not only where we work but how we live.

Several factors lie behind the trend. Faster internet and better collaboration tools let people do office work almost anywhere. Employees value the time saved on commuting and the freedom to arrange their day. Companies have also found that remote work cuts office costs and lets them hire talent from far away.

The benefits, however, come with costs. Working at home blurs the line between work and rest, and some employees find themselves answering messages long after dinner. New staff may learn little about company culture, and casual conversations that once produced ideas may disappear. Isolation is another risk, especially for those who live alone.

The lesson is that remote work is a tool rather than a solution. With clear rules, proper equipment and regular contact, the benefits can outweigh the drawbacks. The future of work is likely to be a mixture of the office and the home, not one replacing the other.
keyPoints: 第一段描述图表趋势，并点明其意义不只是工作地点变化。
第二段从技术、员工和公司三个角度分析原因。
第三段用 however 转折，指出远程办公的代价。
结尾给出条件式结论，避免绝对化。

items.title: Finding Opportunity in Difficulty
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the saying 'In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity.' You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
The remark that in the middle of difficulty lies opportunity is easy to repeat and hard to believe. Yet history and everyday life both suggest that it is true more often than we expect.

A difficulty forces us to stop and look at our situation honestly. When a familiar method fails, we are pushed to learn a new one; when a plan is ruined, we are forced to ask what we really want. Many people discover a talent or a new career only because something they relied on was taken away. The crisis itself is not good, but the change of direction it brings can be.

This view is not a reason to be careless about hardship. Suffering should not be romanticised, and those in trouble need help, not advice. What the remark offers is a way of facing difficulty, not a way of ignoring it. Instead of asking why this happened to me, we can ask what this situation makes possible. That question does not remove the pain, but it turns a dead end into a starting point.
keyPoints: 开头承认名言“说起来容易”，再转向其合理性，形成张力。
用“旧方法失效”“计划被打乱”两个场景说明转向的可能。
第三段澄清观点：不是美化苦难，而是改变提问方式。
结尾用 remove the pain / turns a dead end into a starting point 收束。

items.title: A Shorter Working Week?
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on whether a shorter working week would benefit both employees and employers. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
Proposals for a four-day working week have attracted attention in many countries. I believe a shorter week could benefit both sides, provided that pay and productivity are handled thoughtfully.

For employees, the gain is obvious. Less time at work means more time for family, rest and personal interests, and a well-rested worker is usually healthier and more focused. Experience in some companies suggests that people waste less time when working hours are reduced, because they plan their tasks more carefully. For employers, the reward is a more loyal and energetic workforce, and fewer days of sick leave caused by exhaustion.

The risks, however, are real. Some businesses depend on continuous service and cannot simply close an extra day. Others may try to compress five days of work into four, which would leave employees exhausted rather than refreshed. Small firms, in particular, may struggle to hire additional staff to cover the gap.

In my view, the shorter week is worth trying, but it should be introduced gradually and evaluated honestly. It works best when the goal is better work, not merely less work.
keyPoints: 首段亮明立场：有条件地支持缩短工作周。
第二段分别从员工和雇主角度说明收益，注意 provided that 的用法。
第三段指出真实风险，尤其是小企业的用人压力。
结论强调“逐步推行、认真评估”，避免空喊口号。

items.title: Second-Hand Shopping
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the chart below, which shows that the value of second-hand goods traded online in China has risen sharply over the past six years. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
The chart shows a sharp rise in the value of second-hand goods traded online in China over the past six years. This trend tells us something interesting about how young consumers think.

Several forces are at work. Online platforms have made it much easier to photograph an unwanted item, set a price and reach buyers in other cities. Attitudes have changed: owning second-hand things is no longer regarded as a sign of poverty but as a sensible and even fashionable choice. Young people in particular care about value for money and about waste, and a used laptop or a nearly new coat fits both. Rising prices for new goods push many households the same way.

The effects go beyond individual wallets. Every second-hand transaction keeps a product in use for longer, cutting demand for new materials and the waste that follows. It also encourages people to look after their possessions, because an object that can be sold still has value.

Of course, second-hand trade needs trust. Sellers must describe goods honestly, and platforms must protect buyers. With clear rules, this quiet change in shopping habits can benefit consumers and the environment at the same time.
keyPoints: 第一段概括图表趋势，并指出其反映消费观念变化。
第二段分析技术与观念两方面的原因，用 be no longer regarded as 结构。
第三段把话题从个人省钱提升到资源与环境层面。
结尾补充“信任”这一前提，使论证更完整。

items.title: No One Can Make You Feel Inferior
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the saying 'No one can make you feel inferior without your consent.' You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
The remark that no one can make you feel inferior without your consent places the power of self-worth in our own hands. It does not deny that other people can be cruel; it insists that their judgement needs our agreement before it can wound us.

This idea is easy to accept in theory and difficult to practise. A careless comment about our appearance or our accent can stay in the mind for years. What matters, then, is not only what is said but how much authority we give it. The student who treats a low mark as evidence of failure and the one who treats it as information hear the same result but give it different power.

To withhold consent is not to pretend that criticism never hurts. It means asking whether a judgement is true, and whether it says more about the speaker than about us. Some criticism deserves attention and change; much of it deserves to be let go.

Self-worth built in this way is not arrogance but steadiness. If we refuse to hand our confidence to passing opinions, we can listen and still respect ourselves.
keyPoints: 开头解释名言：自尊的决定权在自己手里。
第二段承认理念易说难行，并用“低分”反应作对比。
第三段澄清“不认同”不等于“不接受批评”。
结尾区分自信与傲慢，收束观点。

items.title: Should Museums Be Free?
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on whether museums and art galleries should be free of charge. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
Whether museums and art galleries should be free of charge is a question about who culture belongs to. In my opinion, the answer is yes, although the arrangement must be designed with care.

The case for free admission rests on the purpose of a public museum. A collection held in the name of the public should be open to the public, not only to those who can afford a ticket. A price on the door keeps out exactly those who might benefit most: students, large families and older visitors. Free entry turns a museum into an ordinary part of city life, a place people can drop into for half an hour rather than a special occasion that must be planned and paid for. Children who grow up visiting museums freely are more likely to keep the habit as adults.

The objections deserve a hearing. Free entry can lead to crowding, and museums still face the cost of staff, security and conservation. One solution is to keep permanent collections free, charge for special exhibitions and rely on public funding and donations.

In short, free admission is not a luxury but a sensible investment in a society's cultural life.
keyPoints: 开头把票价问题提升为“文化属于谁”的问题，立意更高。
用 students, large families and older visitors 具体说明受益人群。
第三段承认反对意见并给出折中方案（常设展免费、特展收费）。
结尾作出明确判断，呼应首段。

items.title: Where Households Spend Their Money
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the chart below, which shows how the spending of Chinese households has changed over the past twenty years: the share spent on food has fallen, while the share spent on education, travel and health has risen. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
The chart records a quiet but important change in Chinese family budgets over the past twenty years: the share of spending on food has fallen, while the share devoted to education, travel and health has risen.

This change is closely linked to rising incomes. When a family earns just enough to cover basic needs, most of the money goes on food. As income grows, the stomach is satisfied first and the remaining money can be spent elsewhere. Parents who once worried about whether their children would eat well now worry about which courses will help them most. People also spend more on health, not because they are iller but because they hope to live longer and better.

The shift has consequences for the economy. Services such as education, tourism and medical care become a larger part of national output, creating jobs that require different skills. It also brings new pressures: school fees and medical bills can be heavy for ordinary families, and saving for them has become a common worry.

Overall, the chart describes something more than numbers. It shows a society moving from having enough to living better, and reminds us that such progress must be shared.
keyPoints: 第一段概括两张图表的反向变化：食品占比下降、教育旅游医疗上升。
第二段用收入增长解释变化，避免只描述不分析。
第三段指出对经济结构的影响与家庭的新压力。
结尾把数据上升为“从吃饱到生活更好”的社会判断。

items.title: Creating the Future
items.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the saying 'The best way to predict the future is to create it.' You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
items.reference:
The remark that the best way to predict the future is to create it challenges a habit many of us share: waiting for events to unfold and then reacting to them. It suggests that the future is not simply discovered but made.

No one can control every circumstance, and plans often fail. What the remark recommends is a shift of attention from prediction to action. Instead of asking what will happen, we can ask what we want to happen and what small step would move us towards it. A student who spends months worrying about the job market gains little; one who learns a practical skill begins to shape his own chances. A community that complains about a neglected park changes nothing, while neighbours who plant a few trees change the place they live in.

The idea also offers comfort. When the future looks uncertain, action is a better remedy than anxiety: it gives us something to do and often reveals possibilities that planning alone could not see. We cannot know what the coming years will bring, but we can decide what part of them we help to build.
keyPoints: 开头改写名言并指出其针对“等待型”心态，论点清晰。
用学生求职与社区种树两个例子，兼顾个人与集体层面。
第三段补充心理层面的价值：行动缓解焦虑。
结尾用 we can decide what part of them we help to build 呼应标题。
